Except for the changes noted in the description above, the form of the figure is exactly that of the Naples statue. Other versions of the same lost original differ slightly from each other in proportions and pose. I have not tried to figure out what the precise measurements and exact pose of the lost original were. I have just used the Naples statue as is, and converted it to bronze.

I have made the color of bronze quite brown. The original may well have been lighter, or yellower, or redder. The tone I have chosen was selected partly because it made the 3D form of the digital model more easily discernible. I have imagined that the statue is a few years old, and has darkened a bit with age. I have also added some weathering and streaks, as though it has been out in the rain. Again, I've done that partly to make the 3D form of the statue easier to make out. I have not done anything about the eyes, which, in the original, would have been made of naturalistic colored materials, as in the Riace Warriors, for example.

Regarding the spear: Assuming that this statue originally held a spear of some sort (as is generally believed), I have chosen to make is a long "dory" rather than a short "akontion." The Doryphoros-with-horse funerary relief from Argos shows a figure carrying an akontion. Most reconstructions of the Doryphoros, however, show the figure with a dory (in keeping with the name for this statue type). On the advice of Dr. Lovisetto, I have opted for the dory. And finally - finish the models so that they don't break immersion when viewing from other angles. All these scenes are great but the way you presented them makes it almost impossible to full appreciate.
Keep up the good work!
